transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because my sleep has just gotten really unreliable lately. Even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I just lie there replaying sales forecasts and team issues in my head. And then, if I do fall asleep, I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again to go back to sleep.
How long have these sleep problems been going on?
Well, it's been a while now. I'd say it's really been building since we had a reorganization in the sales division... so that was about thirteen months ago.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I'm definitely exhausted from the lack of sleep, but I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or down. I still want to do the things I normally enjoy when I actually have the energy for them. It's more just... feeling constantly wound up because my brain won't stop running, rather than feeling sad.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about work-related issues, even when you're not at work?

Yeah, definitely. Most days my mind just... jumps around. I'll start off worrying about whether we'll hit the launch numbers, and then I'm stressing over whether someone on my team is about to quit. And it doesn't stay at work, either. It'll shift to thinking about the mortgage, or a client renewal. I mean, it just feels like every small delay could turn into something major, and I can't seem to shut it off.
Do you ever feel physically restless, tense, or fatigued as a result of all this worrying?

Yeah, I do. I feel... well, I just feel wound up almost all the time. It's honestly like I'm sitting in a stressful pipeline review even when I'm just at home eating dinner. And physically, my shoulders just stay tight. It doesn't really matter how much I try to relax or shake it out, the tension is just always there.
Do you feel like you have trouble controlling your worrying, even when you try to stop thinking about these things?

Yeah, I really do. I try to stop it, I really do. I can tell myself, you know, "Brenda, you've done the plan, just let it go." But... it doesn't last. Maybe five minutes later, I'm right back in another loop. It's like I'll check one concern off my list only to have three more pop up right behind it. I just can't seem to make it stop.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or easily annoyed, especially when you're feeling this constant worry or tension?

Yeah, I have. Um, I've actually started snapping at my reps at work over really minor things, like small CRM updates. And it happens at home, too. I'll get annoyed at my husband over little things, like... just dishes left in the sink. Afterward, I always know my reaction was way bigger than the situation actually warranted, but in the moment, I just get so aggravated.
Have you ever experienced physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when you're feeling especially anxious or worried?

No, not really. I mean, my heart doesn't race or anything like that. I don't really get sweaty or start shaking. It's more just that constant tightness in my shoulders and feeling wound up, like I mentioned. But no, none of those other physical things.
Have you found it hard to focus or concentrate on tasks because your mind keeps drifting to these worries?

Um, no, not really. I actually do okay with concentrating. Even when my mind is kind of spinning with all those other thoughts, I can usually still lock in on whatever task I need to get done for work. It doesn't really pull me away from focusing on what's right in front of me, so I haven't really had an issue with that.
Have there been times when you felt like nothing could cheer you up, or that you were better off dead, even if just fleetingly?

No, I haven't. I mean, I definitely get stressed and overwhelmed with all the worrying, but I've never felt like nothing could cheer me up or... or anything like being better off dead. It's never gone to that kind of dark place. Just the constant worrying, really.
Have you noticed any days where you feel little pleasure or joy, even in activities that usually make you happy?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy the things I usually like doing. I mean, even if I'm having a really stressful week with work and feeling pretty wound up, if I do something fun or relax, I still feel happy. I haven't really lost interest in things or felt that way, no.
Do you often have trouble falling asleep because your mind is racing with thoughts, even if you’re physically tired?

Yeah, actually, that's a big part of why I decided to come in. My sleep has just gotten so unreliable lately. I can go to bed completely exhausted, but I'll just lie there awake, replaying sales forecasts or stressing about team issues at work. And then, even if I do manage to fall asleep, I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight, such as eating more or less than usual or significant weight gain or loss, when you're feeling this way?
No, my appetite has been pretty normal. I haven't noticed any changes in my weight or how much I'm eating. I still eat regular meals, even when I'm feeling really stressed out.
Have you had days where you feel down or tearful, even if it's not necessarily tied to any specific worry or stressor?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had days where I just feel sad or want to cry out of nowhere. It's really just the stress and being so keyed up about work stuff, but I wouldn't say I feel down.
Have you noticed yourself feeling fatigued or having low energy nearly every day, even when you're not physically tired?

I mean, I'm definitely tired during the day, but I think that's just because of the lack of sleep I mentioned. It's not really a general low energy or anything like that. Once I get to the office and start dealing with my team, I'm actually pretty wired and running on adrenaline. So... no, I don't think I feel fatigued out of nowhere, just the normal exhaustion from being awake half the night.
Have you noticed yourself feeling anxious or on edge even when there isn’t anything specific at work or home that you’re worried about?

Yeah, I definitely do. I just feel wound up almost all the time, honestly. It's like... even when I'm just at home eating dinner and there's nothing specific going on, I still feel like I'm sitting right in the middle of a stressful pipeline review. And physically, my shoulders just stay tight no matter how much I try to relax. I just can't seem to turn that on-edge feeling off.
